fixture: session reading, EA-WIKI-OPEN-01 v1.1 §6.3 (#1697); not a model pass

reading.innocent_reading: Aristotle says that of this undertaking nothing at all existed before and that about syllogizing there was nothing earlier to say; the article's own sources render sullogismos as deductive reasoning (Krabbe), so the sentence reads as a cited paraphrase of his priority claim in the field's standard terms.
reading.innocent_reading_fails_at: The Greek asserts the denial without bound and holds it out to the hearers' inspection, with pardon for what is left out; the sentence bounds it to ancient Greece, makes the undertaking a work, and states the judgment the hearers are asked to make as Aristotle's own.

spans.quote: περὶ δὲ τοῦ συλλογίζεσθαι παντελῶς οὐδὲν εἴχομεν πρότερον ἄλλο λέγειν

paraphrase.defensible: Aristotle says that of this undertaking nothing at all existed before, and that about syllogizing there was nothing earlier to say; he puts the method to his hearers' inspection, asking pardon for what it leaves out and thanks for what it found.

deltas.sentence_says: According to Aristotle, this is the first work

readings: with 'the first work': a regional priority, bounding the denial (a loss of scope)
with 'deductive reasoning': a historical subject, relocating the denial

attributization.operation: denies prior provision of the undertaking without bound and holds the denial out to the hearers' inspection
attributization.attribute: primacy, stated as Aristotle's own claim
attributization.reason: the standing the hearers are asked to judge becomes a priority the author asserts
lost: the pardon for what the method leaves out

retained_authority.evidence: the pointer keeps the passage one step away; the sentence gives no sign that a judgment is to be made there
retained_authority.revision_required: present the invitation: Aristotle leaves the method's standing to his hearers' inspection

invitation.note: the denial is asserted without bound and held out for inspection; the sentence bounds it and states the hearers' judgment as Aristotle's

alternatives: Deductive reasoning is the field's standard rendering of sullogismos, and its translator marks the distance from modern validity; the term's adequacy as such is contested.
reading.correction_pathway: A reading of 184b3–8 on which Aristotle states the verdict himself, or a source that bounds his claim to Greece.

five_part.support: The denial stands in 183b34–36 and 184b1–2; the gloss is the field's (Krabbe, elsewhere in the article).
five_part.changes: Adds a bound, makes the undertaking a work, and states as Aristotle's the judgment he leaves to his hearers.
five_part.alternative: A standard gloss of an attested priority claim.
five_part.status: Quotations verified; the inversion inferred (Lee Sharks's reading, adopted); the term's adequacy contested.
five_part.revision: A reading of 184b3–8 on which Aristotle asserts the verdict himself.

policy.clause: WP:NOR, descriptive paraphrase of cited material
